predeclared: 2026-11-05, written before any v2b training run; changes after seeing results must go into a new config
examples: one example per (request, fold budget) reference answer; train split for fitting, validation split for checkpoint selection, test split evaluated once at the end

inputs.note: box length and height are sorted because a box and its swapped partner are the same problem (D30); box width and sheet width only decide feasibility and are not inputs

outputs.foldCount: 12-way classification (0..11 folds), restricted to at most the budget at prediction time
outputs.panels: 11 stick-breaking fractions in [0, 1] (each panel at least 5% of sheet length); the first (folds) are used
outputs.angles: 11 values in [0, 1] mapped to 1..180 degrees; the first (folds) are used
outputs.placement: not predicted: the predicted shape is placed with the same deterministic placement search as the reference (wall placement)

loss: cross-entropy(fold count) + mean squared error on the used panel fractions + mean squared error on the used angles, with the true fold count (teacher forcing)
checkpointSelection: every 50 epochs: validation pass rate from the Node reference checker (valid + fits after placement, 721 motion states); best pass rate wins, ties broken by lower validation loss; stop after 600 epochs without improvement
successCriterion: D20: share of test (request, budget) answers whose predicted design passes all hard rules; the user judges a visual sample. Reference point 95%.
reportedAlongside: all creases on walls (D34) and opening angle relative to the reference answer
fold count equal to the reference
baselines on the same test answers: hand rule (fold-budget-agnostic), nearest-neighbour copy of the closest training answer with the same budget, reference solver
test answers needing more folds than any training answer reported separately (known split imbalance)
ceiling: Decoded reference labels (perfect imitation) pass 4,343/4,359 training answers (99.6%); the 16 failures are zero-slack fits that tip over by floating-point decoding error. This is the ceiling for imitation in this output format.
